summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, portal vein thrombosis, and treated hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted for worsening dyspnea due to a recurrent right pleural effusion. He also reported increasing abdominal distension from ascites. Imaging confirmed a large pleural effusion and moderate ascites, with stable findings in the liver and portal vein. He underwent a therapeutic thoracentesis, removing 3.35 liters of fluid, and a paracentesis, removing 1.1 liters, both without complications. Albumin was given post-thoracentesis. His nadolol was held due to hypotension but restarted at discharge. Warfarin was resumed at a reduced dose of 1.5 mg daily. Labs showed stable liver function, mild hyponatremia, and a rise in creatinine consistent with hepatorenal syndrome. He improved clinically, with resolution of dyspnea and edema, and was discharged home with follow-up for transplant evaluation and INR monitoring.
